qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left) Subject:

On 22 October 2026, former presidential candidate of Ecuador and leader of the Revolución Ciudadana party, Luisa González, was arrested by security forces run by the Daniel Noboa Government. Her arrest comes just a few weeks after local elections were held in Ecuador and follows on from a series of events including the suspension of Revolución Ciudadana, González’s exclusion from standing, growing militarisation and the persecution of social movements – proof of the Noboa Government’s alarming crackdown on the political freedoms and fundamental rights of the country’s political opposition. 1.

Does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy consider that the political freedoms and fundamental rights of the leaders and members of Revolución Ciudadana in Ecuador are sufficiently protected and respected by the current government authorities?

Does she take the view that maintaining preferential trade and diplomatic relations with the Republic of Ecuador, in this context of infringement of rights, could constitute a breach of Article 24 TEU?
Has the Commission considered suspending the trade agreement with Ecuador in response to these breaches of law?
